title: Udaan posts Rs 5,134 Cr gross revenue and Rs 852 Cr loss in FY26
summary:
After a 20% decline in FY25, the B2B ecommerce platform Udaan returned to revenue growth, posting 12.6% year-on-year growth in FY26. The Bengaluru-based company also narrowed its losses by 19% to Rs 852 crore.
Udaan’s gross revenue (GMV) grew to Rs 5,134 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,561 crore in FY25, according to the company’s consolidated financial statements filed by its group company, Trustroot Internet in Singapore.

Founded in 2016 by former Flipkart executives Vaibhav Gupta, Sujeet Kumar and Amod Malviya, Udaan connects brands and wholesalers with retailers through its B2B ecommerce platform, with revenue from goods sales, logistics, platform fees, credit services and advertising.
Udaan’s gross merchandise value (GMV) stood at around Rs 10,000 crore in FY22. The decline since then reflects its exit from non-core categories such as lifestyle and general merchandise, as the company shifted its focus to groceries and essential goods.
On the cost side, material expenses rose 11.3% to Rs 4,859 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,367 crore in the previous fiscal. Finance costs increased 33.5% to Rs 247 crore, while logistics expenses grew 16.7% to Rs 182 crore.
Employee benefit expenses declined to Rs 347.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 500 crore in FY25, largely due to a reduction in ESOP expenses from Rs 280 crore to Rs 140 crore.
Decent revenue growth and lower ESOP costs helped Udaan narrow its net loss by 19.2% to Rs 852 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,055 crore in FY25. This extended its streak of annual loss reduction to four years, from Rs 2,075 crore in FY23 and Rs 1,674.1 crore in FY24.
In September 2026, Udaan agreed to acquire Swiggy’s retail distribution business Lynk Logistics for Rs 500 crore to expand its reach across key markets. Swiggy will receive an approximately 2.8% stake in Udaan through preference shares and invest another Rs 75 crore for a 0.4% stake. The deal will add Lynk’s brand partnerships and retail network to Udaan’s distribution business.
In March this year, Udaan’s parent Trustroot acquired Info Edge’s entire 26.14% stake in Shopkirana for $32.97 million. In exchange, Info Edge received preference shares representing a 2.02% stake in Trustroot and committed an additional $1.72 million, taking its shareholding in Trustroot to 2.13% on a fully diluted basis.
Udaan has also announced a structured financing transaction worth approximately $160 million, as the company looks to strengthen its balance sheet and simplify its capital structure ahead of its long term public market plans.
The company has also been preparing for a public listing and is reportedly expected to achieve profitability by the end of 2027 or the first quarter of 2028 ahead of its planned IPO. The shift of the economy to a rising interest rate cycle might just put paid to those plans, as growth and capital both become dearer. The state of the capital markets post the Jio IPO is also something that is up in the air frankly, unless there is a significant change on the macros. That leaves Udaan in a very interesting situation really, where growth will come from increasing share from weaker players in they are still around. Of course, many would argue that Udaan itself is the player most susceptible to ceding ground as the market toughens up.

title: Zetwerk’s strong anchor book signals global confidence
summary:
Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses has attracted a strong mix of global asset managers, sovereign wealth funds and domestic institutions to its Rs 2,251 crore anchor book ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), with Capital Group emerging as one of the notable names in the allocation.
Two arms of Capital Group — Capital Research and Capital World — received an allocation worth around Rs 288 crore, accounting for nearly 12.88% of the total anchor book. The US-based asset manager is among the largest active investment managers globally, making its participation a key highlight of Zetwerk’s anchor allocation.
The anchor book also saw participation from 3P India Equity Fund, founded by veteran investor Prashant Jain, who previously headed investments at HDFC Mutual Fund for nearly three decades. His participation adds to the domestic investor interest in Zetwerk’s IPO.
The round also saw participation from some of the biggest names in global investing, including BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Nomura, Société Générale, First State, Loomis Sayles, Manulife, Carmignac, Eastspring Investments, Susquehanna and Prudential Assurance.
Sovereign wealth funds also participated in the anchor book, including Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA). Both are long-term institutional investors that invest across markets and asset classes.
The company allotted 14.91 crore equity shares to 99 anchor investors at Rs 151 apiece, the upper end of its price band. The anchor book accounts for around 45% of its Rs 5,012 crore IPO.
Domestic institutions accounted for a significant share of the allocation. Twenty-two mutual funds were allotted around 45.6% of the anchor book, worth approximately Rs 1,027 crore. These included SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset, and Franklin Templeton. Seven life insurance companies, including SBI Life Insurance, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance and Axis Max Life Insurance, also participated.
The breadth of participation is notable as global asset managers, sovereign wealth funds, mutual funds and insurers operate under different mandates and assess investment risks differently. Their participation ahead of the public issue, at the upper end of the price band, points to institutional interest in Zetwerk’s IPO.
Zetwerk’s IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 14.45 crore shares worth around Rs 2,182 crore.
Founded in 2018, Zetwerk operates a manufacturing platform serving sectors such as renewable energy, consumer electronics, aerospace, defence and industrial automation. Its revenue from operations rose 55.4% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore in Q1 FY27, while its loss from continuing operations narrowed to Rs 64.1 crore. The company is backed by investors including Khosla Ventures, Greenoaks, Baillie Gifford, Rakesh Gangwal, Accel, Peak XV and Lightspeed.

title: Tonbo Imaging raises Rs 255 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
summary:
Bengaluru-based defence technology startup Tonbo Imaging has raised Rs 255.36 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), which opens for subscription on October 15.
The company allotted 36.48 lakh equity shares at Rs 700 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band. The anchor book saw participation from global investors such as BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Temasek Holdings, Allianz Global Investors and Prudential, along with domestic mutual funds and insurance companies. SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund were among the domestic investors.
Tonbo Imaging has fixed a price band of Rs 665-700 per share for its Rs 852.2 crore IPO, which will close on October 19. The public issue comprises an offer for sale (OFS) of around 1.22 crore shares by existing shareholders, with no fresh issue component.
Founded by Ankit Kumar, Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar and Cecilia D'Souza, Tonbo Imaging develops imaging and surveillance systems for defence and security applications. Its products include thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, targeting systems, missile seekers and fire control systems.
The company supplies its products to government and defence agencies and operates in the defence electronics segment, which has gained attention amid India's push to strengthen domestic defence manufacturing. 
JM Financial and IIFL Capital Services are managing the IPO. The company's shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE.
Tonbo Imaging’s revenue fell 22.7% to Rs 362.65 crore in FY26, while net profit declined 30% to Rs 50.88 crore. In the June quarter of FY27, it reported a loss of Rs 17.74 crore on revenue of Rs 36.01 crore.

title: Banaraswala raises $2 Mn from Prax Impex to expand across India

title: IntrCity SmartBus’ FY26 revenue rises 40% to Rs 691 Cr; losses rise 76%
summary:
Travel-tech platform IntrCity Smartbus, reported a 40.1% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in FY26, following a Rs 250 crore Series D round led by A91 Partners in October 2025 to support expansion and technology upgrades. However, its losses widened 76% to Rs 28 crore during the year.
IntrCity’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 690.9 crore during FY26 as compared to Rs 493.2 crore in FY25, as per the company’s consolidated financial statements with the Registrar of Companies.

IntrCity SmartBus offers intercity bus travel through its digital platform and a network of independent operators, with services such as live tracking, onboard captains and boarding lounges. It also operates RailYatri, a train travel information and services platform, and relies on rented vehicles and operator partnerships rather than owning its fleet.
Bus operations remained the largest contributor to revenue at Rs 670.35 crore, or about 97% of operating revenue in FY26. Revenue from this service increased 42.5% from Rs 470.56 crore in FY25 as the company expanded its core intercity travel business.
Commission income declined 23.6% to Rs 14.18 crore from Rs 18.55 crore in the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, revenue from advertisement services nearly doubled to Rs 2.44 crore from Rs 1.27 crore.
Including other operating and non-operating income, Intrcity’s total income stood at Rs 693.6 crore in FY26.
On the expense side, bus operations costs rose 43.5% to Rs 539.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 376.13 crore in FY25. The expense accounted for nearly 75% of total costs, in line with IntrCity's asset-light model that relies on rented vehicles and partner operators.
Commissions paid to selling agents increased 51% to Rs 75.97 crore from Rs 50.35 crore. These payments support ticket distribution and customer acquisition through sales agents and booking partners.
Employee benefit expenses grew 8% year-on-year to Rs 49.85 crore from Rs 46.17 crore while advertisement expenses stood at Rs 15.9 crore.
Legal and professional expenses, repair and maintenance costs, payment gateway charges, IT expenses and other overheads drove total expenses by 41% year-on-year to Rs 722.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 512.2 crore in FY25.
The company's EBITDA loss widened to Rs 27.69 crore in FY26 from Rs 16 crore in FY25, while its EBITDA margin deteriorated to -4% from -3.2%.

As operating costs grew faster than revenue, the company's losses widened 76% to Rs 27.9 crore in FY26. On a unit level, IntrCity spent Rs 1.05 to earn an operating revenue during the said period.
Despite the increase in losses, cash and bank balances rose to Rs 49 crore at the end of FY26 from Rs 21 crore a year earlier. Current assets also increased to Rs 62.5 crore from Rs 32.6 crore.
It competes with Abhibus, Zingbus, Leafybus and ixigo’s Freshbus.
While the bus segment is seeing an obvious rise as highway networks improve and people seek more flexibility on availability and pricing, Intercity’s Railyatri platform seems to be at serious risk as AI search answers more and more questions without the need to visit sites. That will be disappointing for the firm that surely expected more from it even two years back. There is probably a case for the firm to assess its priorities even more sharply in terms of the bus booking business,  and see how that can be maximised. Railyatri in fact needs to be repurposed as a platform to track train tickets availability and alternate bus routes exclusively in our view, to ensure the legacy traffic and strength is not frittered away.

title: Figma unveils AI-powered tools to bring code, design and agents onto a single canvas
summary:
Figma has announced a series of product updates aimed at bringing design, code and AI agents together on a single collaborative platform, as the company looks to simplify product development workflows for designers, developers and product managers.
Announced at Config India in Bengaluru, the updates introduce code layers, Figma Specs, centralised design system management and deeper integration with Payload, an open-source backend framework and content management system (CMS).
The company has also expanded its Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem with 20 new partners, including Sarvam AI, Grok Bot and Open Code. The integrations will enable teams to connect coding agents and other AI tools with Figma’s design environment.
“Figma was the first to introduce the multiplayer canvas for teams to design together. The next evolution is a full-stack creative canvas where teams and agents can build together, from idea to ship, in a visual-first way,” said Dylan Field, co-founder and CEO of Figma.
The announcements come a week after Figma made its AI agent generally available. The company said the new features are designed to help product teams collaborate more effectively as AI tools make software development faster and more accessible.
One of the key announcements is code layers, which allow teams to build, explore, edit and compare code-backed prototypes directly on Figma’s Design canvas. The feature is being launched in open beta.
Users can create code layers by prompting the Figma agent, importing work from GitHub repositories or connecting coding agents through MCP. Teams can also convert existing Figma designs into interactive prototypes to evaluate functionality, accessibility and design consistency before development progresses.
The expanded MCP ecosystem will connect Figma with additional tools, including Sarvam AI, an Indian AI company. The move is aimed at enabling teams to integrate their preferred AI tools and coding agents into their existing design workflows.
Figma has also introduced Figma Specs, a native Markdown editor that enables teams to document product requirements, implementation details and design intent in a shared workspace.
Specs can be created as standalone files or alongside existing work on the canvas. The feature also allows users to reference canvas content and embed FigJam diagrams, code layers and designs, helping teams maintain a common understanding of product requirements.
The company said the tool is intended to give AI agents clearer instructions while helping designers, developers and product managers align on what needs to be built.
Another update introduces a centralised space for managing design systems, bringing design libraries, code libraries and guidelines together. The feature is intended to help teams maintain consistency across brands and products while providing AI agents with a unified source of context.
Figma is also deepening its integration with Payload, which joined the company last year. Payload provides backend infrastructure, content management, media management and APIs for websites and applications.
According to Figma, Payload downloads have grown sixfold over the past 12 months. With the new integration, teams can use Figma Make to build applications and connect them to Payload. This will allow designers to work with real content, marketers to manage it through an administrative panel, and developers to customise applications using Payload’s open-source framework.
Figma said the newly announced product updates will roll out to users over the coming weeks, with availability varying by feature.
The announcements come as Figma expands its presence in India. The company said India is its second-largest active user market globally, with more than 40% of companies in the BSE 100 using its platform as of the second quarter of 2026.
Companies using Figma in India include Airtel, CARS24, Groww, Juspay, Myntra, Swiggy, TCS and Zomato.
Globally, approximately two-thirds of Figma’s monthly active users identified as something other than designers as of Q2 2026, reflecting its adoption across a wider range of roles. Around 85% of its monthly active users were located outside the US, while approximately half of its revenue came from international markets.
Config India, Figma’s flagship conference for product builders, is being held at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre in Bengaluru. The company said more than 30,000 people had registered to attend the event in person and virtually.

title: Space robotics startup Cosmochute raises $1.5 Mn in pre-seed round
summary:
Space robotics startup Cosmochute has raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Accel and Prosus Ventures under the Atoms X programme. IIMA Ventures’ Deep-tech and Aerospace Acceleration Fund, Operators Studio and Chinmayi Muthyala also participated in the round.
Cosmochute is among seven startups selected for the inaugural Atoms X cohort, which was launched earlier this year.
The company will use the proceeds for product development, engineering team expansion and its commercial roadmap, as it prepares for its next phase of growth, Cosmochute said in a press release.
Founded this year by Janhavi Gore, Amit Chowdhary and Dhruv Alok Sangal, Cosmochute is building space robotics infrastructure for the emerging lunar economy. Its first programme, LEAP, is a modular platform designed to support payload transportation and deployment on the Moon.
LEAP combines a modular rover and trailer with standard payload bays, allowing multiple payloads to be integrated into a common mission architecture. The company aims to address the cost and complexity of delivering equipment and payloads to the lunar surface through a standardised approach to lunar transportation and deployment.
The platform is designed to reduce the need for mission specific engineering and make lunar transportation and payload deployment more repeatable.
Cosmochute is setting up its lunar laboratories at IIMA Ventures’ incubation facility. The startup is also working within India’s space technology ecosystem, which includes companies, investors and institutions supporting private participation in the sector.
With LEAP as its first platform, Cosmochute plans to develop capabilities in lunar mobility and space robotics, with potential applications in other in space and terrestrial use cases. The company aims to build infrastructure to support commercial and scientific missions to the Moon.

title: Z47 leads $12.5 Mn Series A round in Confido Health
summary:
Healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Z47, with participation from existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures. The round follows a $10 million Series A round announced in September.
The startup had previously raised $3 million in a seed round led by Together Fund in December 2024.
The proceeds will be used to scale its AI platform for healthcare operations, Confido Health said in a press release.
Founded in 2022 by Chetan Reddy and Vichar Shroff, Confido Health develops AI agents to manage tasks such as appointment scheduling, insurance verification and care coordination. The agents integrate with existing healthcare systems through no-code deployment, with the company claiming a setup time of less than five minutes.
Confido Health said its platform integrates with more than 50 systems, including electronic health records, practice management, phone, billing and fax systems, without requiring healthcare providers to change their existing technology stack.
The company said it operates across more than 1,500 care sites, primarily independent practice groups, in 27 states and serves around 3,200 providers. It added that one in 50 patients can now access their healthcare providers through its AI agents.
The platform uses patient details, referral information and payer requirements collected during intake to manage subsequent tasks such as outreach and scheduling. According to the company, this allows a single interaction to trigger multiple workflows, including referrals, appointments, prescription refills and payments.
Confido Health said it has recorded 15x growth since its previous funding round and achieved AI handle rates of more than 95% across key end-to-end office workflows. It also claims its platform adds capacity equivalent to three to five full-time employees on average within three months of deployment.
The company is targeting specialties such as ophthalmology and optometry, physical therapy, dental care, primary care and community care.

title: Enterprise AI startup Shamrock AI raises $5 Mn led by Endiya Partners
summary:
Shamrock AI, an enterprise AI startup building an agentic assurance platform for large enterprises, has raised $5 million in a seed funding round led by Endiya Partners, with participation from Capria Ventures.
The funds will be used to accelerate product development, expand the team and scale go-to-market efforts, Shamrock AI said in a press release.
Founded in 2026 by Sarat Addanki, Michael (Mick) Gallagher and Anuraag Nallapati, Shamrock AI is developing a platform to help enterprises deploy AI agents across critical business processes. Its platform uses an Enterprise Business Knowledge Graph to connect business processes, systems, data and configurations.
The company is initially focusing on agentic test lifecycle automation for enterprise resource planning (ERP) transformations, including SAP S/4HANA migrations. It plans to expand into data observability and autonomous business process automation.
Headquartered in Shillong, Shamrock AI claims to serve multiple Fortune 500 companies, including a Fortune 100 AI hardware manufacturer and a Fortune 100 healthcare company.
The startup plans to expand its team across India and the US, with 70% to 80% of its workforce expected to be based in India. It also plans to build a client-facing team in the US and expand its presence in the Middle East.

summary:
Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses, a manufacturing platform, has raised Rs 2,251.23 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO).
The company allotted 14.91 crore shares to 99 anchor investors at Rs 151 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band.
Global institutional investors participating in the anchor book included Capital Group, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Nomura, Société Générale, Manulife and Susquehanna. Sovereign wealth funds such as Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) also participated in the allocation.
Among domestic investors, SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund received allocations. Insurance companies including SBI Life Insurance, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Bajaj Life Insurance and Axis Max Life Insurance also participated in the anchor round.
Domestic mutual funds received 6.80 crore shares, while seven life insurance companies were allotted 1.10 crore shares, according to the exchange filing.
Zetwerk’s Rs 5,012 crore IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 14.45 crore shares worth Rs 2,182 crore by existing shareholders.
The Bengaluru-based company has fixed its IPO price band at Rs 143-151 per share, valuing it at around Rs 25,583 crore at the upper end. The company plans to use a portion of the fresh issue proceeds to repay debt, with the remaining funds earmarked for acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.
Zetwerk’s IPO will also provide an exit opportunity to its early investors, with Kae Capital and Kalysta Capital set to earn returns of up to 38X on their investments through the offer for sale (OFS). Lightspeed Venture Partners is the largest selling external shareholder, offloading shares worth Rs 426.9 crore, followed by Peak XV Partners, which is selling shares worth Rs 353.5 crore.

title: Scimplify raises $25 Mn in strategic round led by Hitachi Ventures
summary:
Scimplify, a Bengaluru based advanced materials and specialty chemicals manufacturer, has raised $25 million in a strategic funding round led by Hitachi Ventures.
Accel India, Bertelsmann India Investments, Omnivore and 3one4 Capital also participated in the round. Henkel and Teknor Apex joined as new investors. Both companies are also Scimplify’s customers, while Teknor Apex will serve as a manufacturing partner for its US expansion.
The latest funding takes Scimplify’s total equity capital raised to $80 million. The company plans to use the proceeds to expand its research, processing and manufacturing capabilities in the US, with a focus on materials used in semiconductors, defence, energy and AI infrastructure.
Entrackr had reported on Scimplify’s latest funding and valuation in July.
Founded in 2023 by Sachin Santhosh, Salil Srivastava, Dheeraj Dhingra and Hersh Manek, Scimplify develops manufacturing processes to convert raw materials, industrial waste and laboratory discoveries into high purity materials for commercial applications.
The company combines in house scientists and laboratories with its AI enabled platform, Scinode, to develop materials and scale up their production. Its platform maps more than 500 manufacturing facilities and helps identify suitable production routes, equipment and manufacturing partners.
Scimplify said it has served customers in more than 40 countries. More than 40% of its portfolio is focused on advanced materials for semiconductors, batteries and critical minerals, according to the company.
The startup cited projects across semiconductor chemicals, battery materials and tungsten as examples of its work. In one case, it developed a purification process for a high purity chemical used in semiconductor manufacturing and delivered a sample that passed the customer's process test within two months. In another, it developed a process to recover tungsten from industrial scrap and spent catalysts for a US based metals manufacturer.
The company plans to expand its US based research and process development teams, invest in domestic manufacturing and processing capacity, and add American manufacturing partners. It also plans to secure feedstock for critical metals and rare earth materials.
The latest round comes as Scimplify looks to expand its presence in the US and build local production capabilities for advanced materials that are often processed overseas.

title: Parallel Loop raises $6.6 Mn seed round led by 3one4 Capital
summary:
Parallel Loop, an AI operating partner for mid-market and large enterprises, has raised $6.6 million in a seed funding round led by 3one4 Capital.
Co-founded by Prateek Jogani and Yujun Chean in June this year, Parallel Loop works with enterprises to integrate AI into their existing technology, organisational context and workflows.
The company combines its AI stack with forward-deployed engineers who work alongside client teams to connect existing systems, processes and organisational knowledge, and build AI workflows and applications. Its offerings span three areas.
Its AI Enablement service helps leadership teams identify AI opportunities, define roadmaps and build internal capabilities. The AI Stack provides a secure, governed and modular platform that connects existing systems with organisational context. It supports applications ranging from live dashboards to end-to-end workflows.
The Software Factory brings together forward-deployed engineers and AI agents to work with client teams on modernising legacy systems and building new applications.
Parallel Loop said its AI stack can run in a client’s own cloud environment or on-premises, with data residency configured to meet the client’s requirements. This allows enterprises to retain control over where their data and AI workloads are hosted and who can access them.
The platform supports multiple model providers, including open-weight models, and maintains an audit trail of prompts, responses, context changes and actions. Clients retain ownership of their data, organisational context and client-specific work built for them.
Parallel Loop said it has a team of 30 and serves more than 10 clients across industries and geographies. Its clients include Licious and Havells in India, as well as Tokio Marine Safety Insurance in Thailand.

title: Groww’s equity derivatives revenue falls 14.3% QoQ amid CAS impact
summary:
Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of stockbroking platform Groww, saw its equity derivatives revenue decline 14.3% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) in the September quarter of FY27, with the company attributing most of the fall to SEBI’s new Closing Auction System (CAS).
In its quarterly results, Groww said the decline was in line with the trend seen across the industry following the rollout of CAS on August 3, 2026. The system changed the way closing prices are determined for stocks eligible for futures and options (F&O) trading.
Under CAS, exchanges conduct a closing auction to determine the final price of eligible stocks. The change has affected trading volumes as market participants adjust to the new mechanism.
The new system also creates a gap between cash-market and derivatives trading hours. Continuous trading in eligible stocks ends at 3:15 PM, while equity derivatives continue trading until 3:40 PM. This can make it harder for traders to hedge their positions and manage risk during the closing period.
The impact comes even as Groww reported growth in its overall business. Its parent company posted a consolidated net profit of Rs 725.6 crore in Q2 FY27, up 54% year-on-year, while revenue rose 44% to Rs 1,541 crore from Rs 1,071 crore a year earlier.
The share of equity derivatives in Groww’s revenue also declined to 45% in the September quarter from around 57% a year earlier.
Meanwhile, SEBI has proposed changes to the derivatives settlement mechanism to address concerns around CAS. The regulator is considering separating derivatives settlement prices from the closing auction price, a move that could help normalise trading activity if implemented.
The extent of any recovery in derivatives revenue will depend on the final regulatory framework and how market participants adapt to the changes.

title: Decoding: Boldfit founders retain 78.23% stake after Rs 400 Cr Series B
summary:
KL Rahul-backed sports and fitness brand Boldfit has raised Rs 400 crore in its Series B round from The Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company (formerly Pantomath Capital Management), at a valuation of Rs 4,000 crore. The founders still holds over 78%, a rarity in India’s fitness and wellness segment, where D2C brands typically give up significant equity to investors well before reaching this scale.

Entrackr examined Bengaluru-based company's regulatory filings to decode the company's latest funding round, updated captable, and post-money valuation. 
According to the company's regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, Boldfit's board approved the allotment of 12,783 Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 3,12,926.47 per share, aggregating to approximately Rs 400 crore.

The Bharat Value Fund was the sole investor in the Rs 400 crore funding round.
As per Entrackr estimated, Boldfit's valuation jumped 5.71X to Rs 4,000 crore in its Series B round from Rs 700 crore in Series A.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its nationwide retail presence, invest in product innovation and manufacturing, and selectively pursue inorganic opportunities to strengthen its presence across categories.

Co-founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani and Aasshna Guptaa, Boldfit is an e-commerce platform that offers sports and fitness products across categories such as apparel, fitness equipment, nutrition supplements and accessories. Its portfolio covers sports such as basketball, cycling, football, volleyball, badminton and cricket, with over 400 products.

In November 2024 the company had raised Rs 110 crore in a Series A funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners.

Following the latest Series B allotment, Bharat Value Fund emerged as Boldfit’s largest external shareholder with a 10% stake, followed by Bessemer Venture Partners at 8.63%. Founder Pallav Bihani retains a 77.45% stake in the company, while other co-founder Aasshna Guptaa holds 0.78% stake. Meanwhile Indian cricketer KL Rahul owns 0.03% stake.  


Other Indian sports personalities, including Sania Mirza, Manika Batra and Arshdeep Singh, also hold minority stakes in the company.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Boldfit's operating revenue jumped 2.17X to Rs 304 crore from Rs 140 crore in FY24. Its profit also increased 2.08X to Rs 35 crore in FY25 from Rs 16.82 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Groww makes Rs 725 Cr profit on Rs 1,502 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27
summary:
Digital investment platform Groww reported a strong financial performance in the second quarter of FY27, with its profit growing nearly 54% year-on-year to Rs 725 crore. The company also recorded a 47% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations during the quarter.
According to its financial statement sourced from the NSE, Groww’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,502 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,019 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The company earned an additional Rs 39 crore from other income, taking its total income to Rs 1,540 crore during the quarter. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, operating revenue remained largely flat compared with Rs 1,501 crore in Q1 FY27.
Employee benefits remained as the largest cost component for Groww at Rs 169 crore, representing over 30% of total expenses in Q2 FY27. Finance costs and depreciation expenses stood at Rs 4.7 crore and Rs 18.2 crore, respectively.
Overall, the Lalit Keshre-led firm reported a 28% year-on-year increase in total expenditure to Rs 556 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 433 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
The  Groww’s profit surged 54% year-on-year to Rs 725 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 471 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, profit declined marginally by 2% from Rs 735 crore in Q1 FY27.
Groww continued to dominate India’s stockbroking industry in September, retaining its position as the country’s largest broker with 1.34 crore active clients and a 29.16% market share, according to NSE data. The platform added over 1 lakh active clients during the month and has consistently accounted for more than 60% of the industry’s net client additions each month. 
Zerodha and Angel One ranked second and third, with market shares of 14.73% and 14.65%, respectively. Meanwhile, new emerging broker Sahi for the consecutive month recorded the fastest growth among the top 20 brokers.
As of 1:19 PM (today), Groww’s share is trading at Rs 193.3, giving the company total market capitalization of Rs 1,23,238 crore (around $12.9 billion).

title: Astra Studios and VerSe Innovation launch AI content production alliance
summary:
Astra Studios, backed by Hombale Group, has partnered with VerSe Innovation to launch the Astra-Spark Alliance, an AI-powered content production initiative announced at MIPCOM Cannes on October 12.
The alliance combines AstraLabs, Astra Studios’ technology arm, with VerSe’s SparkStation AI Content Operating System to develop an integrated production platform covering scripting, storyboarding, casting, asset generation, editing, rendering and distribution.
The platform plans  to address continuity challenges in AI-generated video, including consistency in faces, costumes, locations and props across scenes. It will support the production of films, series, animation, visual effects and branded content, with artists and production teams overseeing the creative process.
According to the companies, the technology could reduce production costs by up to 75% and shorten timelines from months to weeks. It offers exports for editing tools including Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro and DaVinci Resolve.
Astra Studios will contribute its production expertise and existing client relationships in visual effects and animation, while VerSe will provide the AI workflow technology. The alliance will also develop original content properties to demonstrate the production model.
VerSe Innovation operates platforms including Dailyhunt, Josh, Magzter and OneIndia. Astra Studios works across animation, visual effects, games art, immersive experiences and branded content.

title: RocketPay raises Rs 10 Cr led by Sandeep Jain and Group
summary:
RocketPay, a digital collections infrastructure platform for lenders, has raised Rs 10 crore in a funding round led by Sandeep Jain and Group. 
The round also saw participation from IPV, LetsVenture, Launch Capital, AVNM Ventures and Navyug Global Ventures, alongside existing investor All In Capital.
The fresh capital will support RocketPay’s expansion from digital collections into recovery infrastructure for lenders. It also plans to expand into technology-enabled recovery of financed devices. 
Founded in 2022 by Rishav Dokania, Arpit Bajpai, Ishan Sharma and Kishor Chabbadiya, RocketPay helps lenders automate collections through tools such as Account Aggregator, NACH and UPI Autopay. Its platform also offers remote locking and unlocking of financed Android devices.
The firm claims to have reported a 10x increase in revenue between FY24 and FY26 and aims to reach an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 100 crore by FY28. Its platform is used by lenders with assets under management ranging from Rs 300 crore to Rs 16,000 crore.
The brand is Trustonic’s authorised APAC partner and has access to its Device Lock Controller technology, which enables device-level locking for financing programmes.
The expansion comes ahead of the RBI framework on device locking as a collateral-enforcement tool for mobile loans, which is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027. According to the company, more than 85 million devices are sold on EMIs annually in India, with the market expected to grow at a 10-12% CAGR between FY26 and FY30.

title: Aum Ventures leads Rs 17 Cr round in OXG Space
summary:
Bengaluru-based spacetech startup OXG Space has raised Rs 17 crore in a funding round led by Aum Ventures through its India Innovation Fund II. 
The round also saw participation from Skyroot Aerospace co-founders Pawan Kumar Chandana and Bharath Daka, and Cosmoserve founder Dr Chiran Phanindra.

These include a Ka-band phased-array antenna targeting an initial 1 Gbps-class link, a deployable mesh reflector for ground connectivity, and a deployable solar array to power computing and communications payloads.
Founded by former ISRO engineers Akash Shetty and Sanjay Gorur, OXG Space is building an orbital network that combines satellite connectivity with in-orbit computing to process Earth observation (EO) data and deliver intelligence in near real time.
Currently, EO satellites typically store imagery until they pass over ground stations, resulting in a delay of 4 to 12 hours between observation and insights. 
The company is targeting defence, intelligence and commercial satellite operators. Its technology is designed to combine data from multiple satellites in orbit, enabling faster analysis of optical, radar and signals-intelligence data.
OXG Space’s founders bring over 17 years of combined experience across India’s space programmes, including spacecraft systems for Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3.

The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its dental technology business across India and Southeast Asia.
The fundraise comes after MakeO announced an agreement to acquire Singapore-based dental care startup Zenyum in February. The acquisition is aimed at expanding its presence across Southeast Asian markets.
In 2025, MakeO acquired Apple Dental, a chain of 20 dental clinics across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, for Rs 10.98 crore through a mix of cash and stock.
Following the acquisitions, MakeO has a network of around 1,100 partner dentists across 10 countries. It also operates more than 60 offline clinical centres and has served over 4 lakh consumers, according to the company.
MakeO operates an aligner planning and manufacturing facility in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), with an annual production capacity of over a million aligners. Its products reach dentists and consumers across more than 150 Indian cities, while the company exports to over 10 countries through the Toothsi and Zenyum networks.
Founded in 2018 by Arpi Mehta, Pravin Shetty, Manjul Jain and Anirudh Kal, MakeO initially launched Toothsi as its clear aligner brand. In September 2022, it brought Toothsi and skincare brand Skinnsi under the MakeO umbrella to offer dental, skin and hair treatments through a single platform.
Before the latest round, MakeO had raised over $100 million from investors including Eight Roads Ventures, 360 ONE Asset and Paramark Ventures. In June 2025, it raised Rs 100 crore from existing investors. In January 2024, the company raised $16 million in a round led by 360 ONE Asset and the investment office of Ashish Kacholia.
MakeO said its combined business has crossed Rs 500 crore in revenue and achieved EBITDA profitability earlier in 2026. The company aims to double its revenue over the next two to three years.

title: Former DealShare CEO Kamaldeep Singh joins Indofast Energy as CEO
summary:
Kamaldeep Singh, former chief executive officer of DealShare, has joined Indofast Energy, a joint venture between Indian Oil Corporation (IndianOil) and SUN Mobility, as its CEO.
Singh announced his new role in a LinkedIn post. He said he would focus on building an energy and mobility platform at a national scale by combining IndianOil’s nationwide presence with SUN Mobility’s technology capabilities.
“I am excited to begin a new chapter as CEO of Indofast Energy,” Singh said. He added that the company aims to simplify the transition to electric mobility by making energy accessible, reliable, convenient and economically viable.
The appointment comes after Singh’s exit from DealShare, which Entrackr exclusively reported in August. Entrackr also reported that the struggling ecommerce startup was in acquisition talks with online pharmacy platform TrueMeds and meat and seafood e-retailer Captain Fresh as it faced the prospect of a shutdown. Talks with TrueMeds were more advanced than those with Captain Fresh, although neither transaction had been finalised at the time.
Singh brings more than 25 years of experience in building and transforming consumer businesses. Before joining DealShare, he served as CEO of Big Bazaar and held leadership roles at Future Group.
Indofast Energy operates in the electric vehicle battery swapping segment. The company is a 50:50 joint venture between IndianOil and SUN Mobility. It combines IndianOil’s nationwide presence with SUN Mobility’s battery swapping technology.
Its battery as a service (BaaS) model allows electric vehicle users to exchange depleted batteries for charged ones, which reduces the time required to recharge vehicles.
As CEO, Singh will lead the company’s efforts to expand its battery swapping network across India, with a focus on business growth and a scalable operating model.
Separately, SUN Mobility has appointed Satish Sundaresan as its CEO. Sundaresan will lead engineering, manufacturing operations and global sourcing, while Singh will oversee Indofast Energy’s operations and expansion.

title: Urban Company to consider fresh fundraise
summary:
Urban Company, the home services marketplace, will consider a proposal to raise fresh funds at a board meeting on October 16, according to its regulatory filing.
The company may raise funds through a QIP, preferential allotment, private placement or other permitted routes, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals. The company has not disclosed the proposed amount in its exchange filing.
According to a Moneycontrol report, Urban Company is looking to raise around Rs 2,000-2,500 crore through a QIP.
The proposed fundraise comes amid rising competition in the instant home services segment, where startups such as Snabbit and Pronto are raising fresh capital to expand their operations.
Snabbit raised $56 million in a Series D funding round in April 2026, led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments and Bertelsmann India Investments. The round valued the startup at around $350 million, taking its total funding to about $112 million.
Meanwhile, Pronto closed its Series B round at $45 million in May 2026, including a $20 million investment from investor Lachy Groom. The round valued the startup at $200 million.
Urban Company also raised $50 million through a fresh issue of shares during its IPO in September 2025. The public issue additionally included an offer for sale of Rs 1,428 crore by existing shareholders.
In Q1 FY27, Urban Company's revenue from operations grew 44% year-on-year to Rs 528 crore. However, the company reported a net loss of Rs 92 crore, against a profit of Rs 6.9 crore in the year-ago period. Its net transaction value increased 42% to Rs 1,465 crore.
The losses came amid continued investments in InstaHelp, its quick-service domestic help business. The segment reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 132 crore during the quarter, while the company's other businesses continued to grow.
The board will decide on the proposed fundraising structure and terms at the October 16 meeting.

title: AI video platform Clueso raises $10 Mn in Series A round led by Dharana Capital
summary:
AI video platform Clueso has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Dharana Capital, with participation from new investors Founders Future and Neotribe Ventures. Existing investors Y Combinator and f7 Ventures also participated in the round.
The latest funding takes the company’s total capital raised to $12 million. According to the company, more than 80% of the Series A capital came from existing investors.
Founded by Akash Anand, Prajwal Prakash and Neel Balar, Clueso provides an AI-powered platform that helps businesses create and update videos for marketing, customer education, onboarding, training and internal operations.
The company said its platform is used by more than 1,000 businesses, including Atlassian, Zendesk, Gainsight, Seismic and Ironclad. According to Clueso, its customers have reported more than fivefold productivity gains and an 80% reduction in video production costs.
Clueso uses AI agents to automate different stages of video production, including capturing software workflows, generating scripts and voiceovers, editing footage and maintaining brand consistency. The platform can also update videos when products or business processes change.
The company also offers integrations with other business tools and support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which allows AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT to create, edit and manage videos through Clueso.
Clueso said it will use the fresh capital to expand its enterprise sales and go-to-market operations, develop its AI agent capabilities, improve editing features and strengthen integrations with business software.
The funding comes amid growing adoption of AI tools across enterprise workflows, including content creation, employee training and customer education. Clueso is focused on automating video production for businesses, with an emphasis on creating and maintaining content as products and processes evolve.

title: Exclusive: StockGro plans Rs 536 Cr IPO fresh issue, to appoint independent directors
summary:
Social investing and stock market advisory platform StockGro’s parent company, AssetGro Fintech, is set to raise Rs 536 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares as part of its proposed initial public offering (IPO). 
 
According to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), AssetGro Fintech Ltd, the parent entity of StockGro, passed a resolution to approve the issue of up to Rs 536 crore in fresh equity and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders. 
 
However, the size of the OFS has not been disclosed in the resolution. According to media reports, StockGro is looking to raise up to Rs 2,000 Cr-Rs 2,500 Cr through the initial public offering.
 
Notably, the company may raise up to Rs 107.2 crore through a pre-IPO placement before the offer. If completed, the amount raised through the placement will be deducted from the fresh issue, the filing further stated.

The company has yet to disclose the final IPO size, price band, valuation or listing timeline.

In a separate filing ahead of its IPO, StockGro has passed a resolution to appoint Dinesh Chander Patwari, Yatrik Rushikesh Vin and Divya Dwivedi as independent directors for five-year terms. The company has also proposed appointing Diyanshi Agrawal as a nominee director.
 
Founded in 2020 by former venture capitalist Ajay Lakhotia, StockGro is building a full-stack ecosystem for smarter trading and investing through expert-driven insights and AI-powered research, delivered via its social-first, community-led platform.
The company has raised over $100 million in funding to date, including investments from BITKRAFT Ventures, SBI Ventures, Root Ventures, and General Catalyst and others.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. Its operating revenue increased 30.99% to Rs 113.33 crore in FY25 from Rs 86.52 crore in FY24. It reported a profit of Rs 34.64 crore in FY25, compared to a loss of Rs 101.17 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A) raises Rs 3,000 Cr for growth-stage AI and deeptech fund
summary:
Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A) has secured Rs 3,000 crore in subscriptions for its growth-stage AI and deeptech investment strategy.
The capital has been raised from Indian and overseas investors through two regulated investment vehicles. Nandan Nilekani has joined the fund as an anchor investor and mentor.
Led by general partners Ashish Kumar, Debraj Banerjee and Vivek Singla, F2A plans to deploy the capital across 12 to 15 companies over the next two to three years. The fund plans to invest Rs 100 crore to Rs 200 crore in each company, with a focus on businesses that have a technological edge and the potential to scale.
F2A will invest across AI-led digital consumer businesses, enterprise software, AI applications, deeptech infrastructure and engineered systems. It will target growth-stage companies that have validated their technology and are expanding their customer base in India and overseas markets.
The fund has also secured investor approvals to increase its overall hard cap amid demand beyond its current capacity. However, the revised target corpus has not been disclosed.
F2A aims to support portfolio companies as they expand operations, build intellectual property and pursue further growth opportunities. The firm also plans to help them access customers, strategic partners and talent.
The fund has secured commitments amid growing investor interest in Indian companies developing AI and frontier technologies. F2A believes India-domiciled businesses can build technology products and intellectual property for domestic and international markets as they move from technology validation to commercial expansion.
The three general partners bring experience working with technology companies at different stages of growth. F2A plans to support founders through the expansion phase by providing capital and access to customers, strategic partnerships and talent. The firm expects its portfolio companies to take a few years to reach public-market readiness, positioning the fund as a growth-stage investor.

title: NPCI defers UPI MDR rollout to post Diwali
summary:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has deferred the implementation of the merchant discount rate (MDR) on select Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions until after Diwali. The revised implementation date will be notified separately.
The decision was taken by the UPI and Services Steering Committee on October 13, keeping the festive season in mind. The framework was originally scheduled to take effect from October 15.
Under the framework announced on September 15, a 0.4% MDR will apply to eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. The charge will be capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above.
Transactions above Rs 2,000 in specified sectors such as railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs will attract a flat MDR of Rs 5. Capital market transactions will attract an MDR of 0.02%, capped at Rs 300 per transaction.
Person-to-person (P2P) transfers and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000 will remain free. Small merchants covered under the person-to-person merchant (P2PM) framework will also continue to be exempt from MDR. According to the government, around 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected by the revised framework. Merchants will not be allowed to pass on the MDR to customers.
The framework aims to support the sustainability of the UPI ecosystem and fund investments in payment infrastructure, security and merchant acceptance networks. The charges will be distributed among participants in the payment ecosystem rather than collected as a tax by the government or NPCI.

title: ThinkMetal raises Rs 27 Cr led by IAN Alpha Fund

Advanced materials and manufacturing startup ThinkMetal has raised Rs 27 crore in a funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from 3i Partners and existing investors. 
The proceeds will be used to develop its products, expand its research and development capabilities, and increase adoption among industrial customers.
Founded by Sabyasachi Ghosh and Arushi Sharma, ThinkMetal is developing indigenous technologies for precision metal manufacturing. Its platform combines advanced materials, manufacturing processes and industrial systems to reduce production time and dependence on imported technologies.
The company’s current commercial offering is SistemT1, a metal additive manufacturing system designed to produce precision metal components. The system uses ThinkMetal’s proprietary FuseX metal filament technology. The company is also expanding its materials library and developing in-house capabilities to process new materials.
ThinkMetal serves manufacturers across aerospace, defence, space, automotive and electric mobility. It has moved from technology development to enterprise pilots and is now working towards larger commercial deployments. According to IAN Alpha Fund, the company has filed more than 17 intellectual property applications.
The company claims its technology can manufacture high-value precision metal parts up to 10 times faster and at half the cost of conventional methods.

The startup is developing a platform to redesign chemical synthesis processes by evaluating raw materials, reaction pathways and process economics.
NuSynth uses predictive synthesis models and an AI engine that processes experimental data to inform future research cycles. Its platform focuses on developing alternative synthesis routes with changes to cost, yield, safety, sustainability and scalability.
The startup is initially focusing on pharmaceuticals and electronics chemicals. It plans to develop proprietary chemical processes for commercial applications across multiple chemistry-led sectors.
The fresh capital will be used to develop its R&D and technology capabilities, build an initial portfolio of proprietary processes, strengthen scale-up capabilities and expand the team.
NuSynth was founded by Poorvank Purohit, former MD and CEO of Solara Active Pharma Sciences, and Dr Ramesha A R, a postdoctoral researcher at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Washington. The founding team also includes Abhishek Deo and Dipak Bajaj, who have worked with companies such as Zetwerk, Mstack, Ola, JPMorgan, BlackBuck and SUN Mobility.
According to the company, its platform is designed to reduce the time required for chemical R&D by using data from previous experiments to guide subsequent research.

title: Qualcomm exits Shadowfax with Rs 157 Cr stake sale
summary:
Qualcomm Ventures has sold Rs 157.28 crore worth of shares in logistics company Shadowfax Technologies through an open market transaction.
Qualcomm Asia Pacific Pte Ltd, an affiliate of the US-based chipmaker, sold 57.13 lakh shares, representing a 0.98% stake, at an average price of Rs 275.30 per share, according to bulk deal data on the BSE.
This follows another stake sale in August, when Qualcomm sold 75 lakh shares, representing a 1.28% stake, for Rs 183.85 crore at an average price of Rs 245.13 per share. Across the two transactions, Qualcomm has sold Shadowfax shares worth around Rs 341 crore.
The investor held a 2.26% stake in Shadowfax at the end of June 2026.
The latest sale comes amid a series of stake sales by existing investors in Shadowfax. TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has also been selling shares in the logistics company through multiple bulk deals.
On October 6, NewQuest sold 40 lakh shares of Shadowfax for Rs 114.8 crore at Rs 287 per share. This was its fourth stake sale in the company in three months. Since July, NewQuest has sold around 2.85 crore shares, reducing its stake by approximately 4.86 percentage points. It held an 11.53% stake at the end of June 2026.
Shadowfax provides logistics services to ecommerce, quick-commerce and direct-to-consumer (D2C) companies. Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Bansal and Vaibhav Khandelwal, the company operates across more than 16,000 pincodes.
The company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 65.4 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 8 crore a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 65% year-on-year to Rs 1,358 crore during the quarter.
Shadowfax shares are currently trading at Rs 296.15 with a total market capitalization of Rs 17,391 crore.

title: Mesa School of Business raises Rs 110 Cr in equity and debt
summary:
Startup-focused business school and edtech company Mesa School of Business has raised Rs 110 crore, comprising around Rs 85 crore in Series A equity funding co-led by Dharana Capital and existing investor Elevation Capital, and Rs 25 crore in venture debt from InnoVen Capital and Alteria Capital.
The company is also backed by founders including Kunal Shah of CRED, Vidit Aatrey and Abhiraj Bhal of Meesho, and Vijay Shekhar Sharma of Paytm.
According to the company, the fresh funding round values it at Rs 385 crore.
Entrackr had exclusively reported on Mesa School of Business’s Series A funding last month.
The proceeds will be used to invest in an AI-first curriculum for existing programmes, launch and scale new programmes, and build strategic partnerships with the startup ecosystem, the company said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2023 by Ankit Agarwal and Varun Limaye, Mesa School of Business offers residential programmes for undergraduates, fresh graduates and early-career professionals. The Bengaluru-based institution aims to prepare students for leadership and entrepreneurship in an AI-first world.
The company said every student builds and runs a small business and learns to use AI to develop and launch a technology product. Mesa has grown from a single postgraduate cohort to over 550 students across three programmes: a one-year Post Graduate Programme in Startup Leadership, a four-year undergraduate programme in business and entrepreneurship, and Forge, a one-year programme for fresh graduates.
Mesa said over 100 founders have taught on campus, while students have worked on more than 200 projects with startups. Its alumni pursue full-time roles at startups or start their own businesses.
According to the company, students from its first two postgraduate cohorts secured an average CTC of Rs 26 lakh, while the top 25% averaged Rs 36.5 lakh. All placed students joined startups, including Zomato, Zepto, Urban Company, Scapia and Comet, with 58% taking up founder-facing roles.
Nearly 20% of graduates have become entrepreneurs, Mesa said. More than 50 student startups are currently incubated at Mesa Startup Lab, its in-house residency programme. These startups have collectively raised over Rs 25 crore in funding and grants and have an annual revenue run-rate of over Rs 50 crore.

title: KL Rahul-backed Boldfit raises over Rs 400 Cr in Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund
summary:
Boldfit, a homegrown sports brand, has raised over Rs 400 crore (nearly $42 million) in its Series B funding round led by Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company Alternates, part of the Pantomath Group. Existing investor Bessemer Venture Partners also participated in the round.
The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised Rs 110 crore, or around $13 million, in a funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners in November 2024. It also raised $8.37 million from existing investors, including KL Rahul.
The fresh funds will be used to drive growth, with investments planned in nationwide retail expansion, product innovation and manufacturing. The company will also selectively pursue inorganic opportunities to strengthen its presence and capabilities across categories, Boldfit said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani and Aasshna Guptaa, Boldfit is an e-commerce platform that offers sports and fitness products across categories such as apparel, fitness equipment, nutrition supplements and accessories. Its portfolio covers sports such as basketball, cycling, football, volleyball, badminton and cricket, with over 400 products.
The company said it serves over 2 crore customers annually. It is also strengthening its integrated product development and manufacturing capabilities, with a focus on innovation, quality and long-term competitive advantages.
Boldfit aims to build a sports brand for a billion Indians through product innovation, manufacturing and nationwide distribution, the company said.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. Its operating revenue jumped 2.17X to Rs 304 crore in FY25 from Rs 140 crore in FY24. Profit also surged 2.08X to Rs 35 crore in FY25 from Rs 16.82 crore in the previous fiscal.
In the sports and fitness segment, Agilitas, a sportswear platform, raised Rs 225 crore from Nexus Venture Partners and Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, in June 2026. The funds will be used to strengthen its manufacturing, brand-building, retail and technology capabilities.
Meanwhile, PlayBlue raised $2.7 million in seed funding in July 2026 from Centre Court Capital, MIXI Global and WEH Ventures to launch its omnichannel sports retail business, which will include a pan-India e-commerce platform and flagship stores.

title: Nazara’s Nitish Mittersain steps down as MD; Mithun Sacheti becomes executive director, Arun Agrawal named CFO
summary:
Nazara Technologies founder Nitish Mittersain will step down as managing director and transition to the role of founder and non executive director, months after stepping down as CEO. The company has also redesignated Mithun Padam Sacheti as an executive director and appointed a new chief financial officer (CFO).
The company’s board approved the changes at a meeting held on October 12, according to a stock exchange disclosure.
Mittersain, who founded Nazara in 1999, will move out of his executive responsibilities as managing director, subject to shareholder approval. He will continue to provide strategic guidance to the company.
In August 2026, Mittersain stepped down as CEO following the company’s Q1 FY27 results, which were hit by losses from associates and impairment charges.
Meanwhile, Nazara has redesignated Sacheti from non executive director to whole time director and key managerial personnel, subject to shareholder approval. Sacheti, the founder of jewellery brand CaratLane, will oversee strategic initiatives and operational responsibilities assigned by the board.
The company has also appointed Arun Agrawal as CFO from October 16, replacing Rakesh Shah, who will step down on October 15 to pursue a professional opportunity outside the company. 
Before joining Nazara, Agrawal served as global CFO at Ness Digital Engineering and held a senior finance role at Mastek. He has also worked with Firstsource Solutions, General Electric, Wipro and Tata Motors.
In another leadership change, whole time director Rohit Sharma will step down from his position with effect from January 11, 2027, to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities.
The leadership changes come as Nazara continues to expand its gaming portfolio. Separately, the board approved an investment of $77 million (around Rs 743 crore) in its UK subsidiary to fund the second tranche of consideration for its acquisitions of Bluetile Games and Bestplay Systems.
The board also approved the allotment of 2.39 crore equity shares at Rs 306 apiece to five investors on a preferential basis, raising around Rs 731 crore. In addition, it approved the conversion of outstanding loans worth up to Rs 129.35 crore extended to Smaaash Entertainment and a £23 million (around Rs 294.4 crore) loan extended to its UK subsidiary into equity.

title: InCred Capital appoints Abhinav Khanna as Capital Markets CEO, Abhimanyu Kalra as MD of Equities
summary:
InCred Capital has appointed Abhinav Khanna as CEO of Capital Markets and Abhimanyu Kalra as managing director and co-head of equities as it looks to expand its institutional equities business in India.
The appointments are part of the company’s efforts to grow its market share in India’s institutional equities segment multi-fold over the next five years, supported by investments in technology, execution infrastructure and international expansion, InCred Capital said in a press release.
Khanna brings over 25 years of experience across India, the UK and the Middle East. He most recently served as managing director and chief business officer at ValueQuest Investment Advisors. Before that, he spent over a decade at Citigroup Global Markets, where he was managing director and head of equities for India.
Kalra has over 23 years of experience in equity markets, including 18 years at Nomura, where he developed relationships with global and domestic asset managers.
The company has also launched its US business under Arunava Das, who joins as CEO of InCred Capital USA. Das previously served as CEO of JM Financial’s North America business and has held senior roles at JPMorgan Chase and Edelweiss Capital.
Alongside the leadership appointments, InCred Capital is investing in technology and execution infrastructure across order management, research distribution, institutional sales and trading, block execution and algorithmic trading.
The platform serves institutional clients, including mutual funds, insurance companies, pension funds, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), global long only investors and hedge funds.
“We are making a big bet on Capital Markets. India’s markets are getting larger, deeper and more important to global investors, while domestic institutional capital continues to grow rapidly,” said Bhupinder Singh, founder and group CEO of InCred.
Singh added that the company aims to build one of India’s leading institutional equities franchises.
InCred Capital is the institutional, wealth management and asset management arm of the InCred Group. It offers services across investment banking, institutional equities, wealth management and asset management.

title: Zetwerk IPO: Early investors set for up to 38X returns through OFS
summary:
Zetwerk’s upcoming IPO is expected to deliver multi-fold returns to several early investors, with Kae Capital and Kalysta Capital set to earn around 38X returns on their investments. The offer for sale (OFS) will see existing shareholders offload 14.45 crore shares worth approximately Rs 2,182 crore.
According to Entrackr’s analysis, Lightspeed Venture Partners is the largest selling external shareholder in Zetwerk’s IPO, with a share sale worth Rs 426.9 crore. At the upper price band of Rs 151 per share, it is set to clock around 4.5X returns based on the average acquisition cost across its participating funds. Peak XV Partners will offload shares worth Rs 353.5 crore, translating into around 9.3X returns, while Accel is set to generate around 19.3X returns on its Rs 181.5 crore share sale.

The average acquisition costs for Lightspeed and Peak XV have been calculated across their respective funds participating in the OFS.
Kae Capital will sell shares worth Rs 189.8 crore through the OFS and is set to clock around 38.3X returns based on an average acquisition cost of Rs 3.94 per share. Kalysta Capital will offload shares worth Rs 63.3 crore, also generating around 38.3X returns at the upper price band.
Among other shareholders, promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload shares worth Rs 346.9 crore. Its acquisition cost of Rs 178.58 per share is higher than the IPO’s upper price band, implying a return of around 0.85X on its investment.
Zetwerk co-founders Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan will each sell shares worth around Rs 214.9 crore. Other OFS participants include Saifuddin Fakhruddin Qureshi and Matthew Harris Arnold, who will sell shares worth Rs 43.1 crore and Rs 36.9 crore, respectively.
Zetwerk’s IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 2,830 crore and an OFS of 14.45 crore shares. The company aims to raise around Rs 5,012 crore through the public issue, valuing it at around Rs 25,583 crore at the upper end of the price band. The IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19, with listing scheduled for October 23.
Founded in 2017, Zetwerk operates a technology-led manufacturing platform that connects businesses with manufacturers and suppliers across sectors such as electronics, energy, aerospace, defence and industrial automation.
Financially, the company’s revenue from continuing operations rose to Rs 15,913 crore in FY26 from Rs 11,332 crore in FY25. In Q1 FY27, revenue from operations grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore, while losses from continuing operations narrowed to Rs 64 crore from Rs 881 crore in the year-ago quarter.

title: Zetwerk sets IPO price band at Rs 143-151; eyes Rs 5,012 Cr from issue
summary:
Manufacturing platform Zetwerk has fixed the price band for its initial public offering (IPO) at Rs 143-151 per share. The Bengaluru-based company aims to raise around Rs 5,012 crore through the public issue, valuing it at around Rs 25,583 crore at the upper end of the price band.
The IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The company will open its anchor investor book on October 14, while its shares are expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 23.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 14.45 crore shares by promoters and existing investors, according to its red herring prospectus (RHP).
Zetwerk has increased the fresh issue size from Rs 2,600 crore proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) filed in August. The OFS component has also increased by 49% from 9.68 crore shares proposed earlier.
Promoters Amrit Pratik Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan will each sell 1.42 crore shares, while promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload up to 2.30 crore shares. Among existing investors, Lightspeed Venture Partners will sell 2.51 crore shares, followed by Peak XV Partners with 2.34 crore shares. Accel India V will also sell up to 1.2 crore shares.
Zetwerk plans to use Rs 1,300 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay borrowings at the company level. Another Rs 860 crore will go towards debt repayment at nine subsidiaries. The remaining proceeds will be used for acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2017, Zetwerk operates a technology-led manufacturing platform that connects businesses with manufacturers and suppliers across sectors such as electronics, energy, aerospace, defence and industrial automation.
On the financial front, Zetwerk’s revenue from continuing operations rose to Rs 15,913 crore in FY26 from Rs 11,332 crore in FY25. In Q1 FY27, revenue from operations grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore, while losses from continuing operations narrowed to Rs 64 crore from Rs 881 crore in the year-ago quarter.

title: Zetwerk raises fresh issue size to Rs 2,830 Cr, OFS component up 49% in RHP
summary:
Manufacturing platform Zetwerk has filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) for its initial public offering (IPO), comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore.
According to its RHP, the Bengaluru-based company has increased its fresh issue size to Rs 2,830 crore from Rs 2,600 crore proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP). The offer for sale (OFS) has also increased by 49% to 14.45 crore shares from 9.68 crore shares proposed in the UDRHP filed in August.
The OFS will include shares from promoters Amrit Pratik Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, who will each sell 1.42 crore shares. Promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload up to 2.30 crore shares. Together, they will offer around 5.14 crore shares.
Among the existing investors, Lightspeed Venture Partners will offload the most, at 2.51 crore shares, followed by Peak XV Partners, which will sell 2.34 crore shares.
Kae Capital Fund and Kalysta Capital Fund will collectively sell up to 1.67 crore shares. Accel India V will also participate in the OFS, offloading up to 1.2 crore shares.
The offer will be open for subscription on October 15, 2026 to October 19, 2026 while anchor bid will start on October 14.
Zetwerk plans to use Rs 1,300 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay borrowings at the company level. Another Rs 860 crore will be used to repay debt at nine subsidiaries. The remaining proceeds will be allocated towards acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2017 by Acharya and Ramakkrushnan, Zetwerk operates a technology-led manufacturing platform that connects businesses with manufacturers and suppliers across sectors such as energy, electronics, aerospace, defence and industrial automation.
On the financial front, Zetwerk’s revenue from continuing operations rose to Rs 15,913 crore in FY26 from Rs 11,332 crore in FY25. In Q1 FY27, revenue from operations grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore, while losses from continuing operations declined 93% to Rs 64 crore from Rs 881 crore in the year-ago quarter.

The partnership aims to simplify self-regulatory organisation (SRO) certification for OTT platforms and online content publishers that use PhonePe’s payment gateway. summary:
Natural personal care D2C firm Nat Habit is raising Rs 142.6 crore ($15 million) in a fresh round led by Trident Growth Partners, with participation from Bertelsmann, Firstport, Linklight Ventures and others.
The board at Nat Habit is issuing 22.5 lakh Series C preference shares at an issue price of Rs 633.5 each to raise Rs 142.6 crore, according to its regulatory filing accessed from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Trident Growth Partners will be leading the round with Rs 91 crore, while Bertelsmann and Linklight Ventures will invest Rs 37 crore and Rs 6.8 crore, respectively. Mirabilis, Firstport and Dharmayug Investments will contribute the remaining amount.
According to the filings, the fresh proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, expansion, brand building and other requirements. Notably, Rs 2.6 crore from the total proceeds will also be used for the reduction of the ESOP pool.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the post-money valuation of the firm stood at around Rs 800 crore.
Moneycontrol reported on Nat Habit’s fresh funding in July.
Following the fresh issue, Trident Growth Partners will hold an 11.44% stake in the company, while existing investor Bertelsmann will hold 17.54% of the cap table. As per the filing, before the fresh issue, Swagatika Das and Gaurav Agarwal held 16% each in the firm.
Nat Habit has rebranded itself as Breathe Life, marking a shift in its positioning from an Ayurvedic brand to a broader lifestyle proposition. The company sells Ayurvedic personal care products, including shampoos, face washes, and moisturisers.
The company is yet to file its annual statements for FY26. During FY25, its revenue from operations grew 47.2% year-on-year to Rs 106 crore, while its losses increased to Rs 29 crore in the same period.

title: OTPless appoints former BharatPe, Genwise exec Geetanshu Singla as CTO
summary:
Bengaluru-based identity and access management startup OTPless has appointed former BharatPe technology head and Genwise co-founder Geetanshu Singla as its Chief Technology Officer (CTO).
In his new role, Singla will lead engineering, product development, platform architecture, reliability and security across OTPless’s authentication and fraud prevention stack, which includes Silent Network Authentication, WhatsApp authentication, device intelligence and passkeys.
Singla was previously Vice President of Technology at BharatPe, where he worked closely with OTPless co-founders Satyam Nathani and Tanmay Sagar during the fintech’s early growth. He later co-founded Genwise, which shut down its operations in December last year.
The appointment follows a series of leadership changes at OTPless. On September 18, the company elevated Nathani as CEO and Sagar as COO. On October 1, it appointed early team member Manas Poddar as Chief Business Officer (CBO).
OTPless claims to authenticate over 300 million users across consumer platforms such as Meesho, Zepto, Navi, PhysicsWallah, ShareChat, Shiprocket and ixigo. The company has grown its topline 2.5X over the past year to Rs 36 crore in annualised revenue and has been break-even for the past two quarters..
“The businesses we serve are some of India’s largest consumer platforms, and for them, login is the front door to their entire business. A failed or slow authentication is a lost customer, so they need technology they can rely on at any scale, on any day. Geetanshu has built and run technology at unicorn scale, and his joining strengthens the technical trust our customers place in us,” said Sagar.
Singla said he had worked closely with Nathani and Sagar during his time at BharatPe and described joining OTPless as coming back home. He added that the company’s expansion from OTP authentication to a broader identity and trust layer presents a significant opportunity.
Founded in 2023, OTPless provides authentication and identity infrastructure to consumer internet companies. Its platform enables user verification through Silent Network Authentication, WhatsApp authentication, device intelligence and passkeys, reducing reliance on SMS-based one-time passwords.
The company has raised over $6 million from investors including Venture Highway, White Venture, FJ Labs, SIDBI and Piper Serica.
